 Flying for Thanksgiving? Your iPhone or Android can now serve as your ID at airport security.
 Apple Wallet and Google Wallet let travelers create a digital ID using a U.S. passport, but there are a few things to know before heading to the airport.
 Remember when you could get through an airport and onto a plane without showing your driver's license?
 These days, getting through airport security often means juggling a carry-on bag while digging through your pockets or purse for identification. But if you're flying for Thanksgiving, your smartphone may make the process a little easier.
 Both iPhone and Android users can now create a digital ID using a valid U.S. passport. It's not a digital driver's license. Instead, it's a secure digital version of your passport information that can be used to verify your identity at participating TSA security checkpoints.
 And you can set it up before leaving home.
 How to set up a digital ID on your iPhone 
 Apple's Digital ID is available through the Wallet app on compatible iPhones.
 Here's how to get started:
 Open the Apple Wallet app.
 Tape the plus (+) sign
 Select Driver's License or ID Cards, then Digital ID.
 Scan the phone page of your valid U.S. passport.
 Hold your iPhone against your passport to read its embedded electronic chip.
 Follow the instructions to complete facial verification, including a video selfie.
 Yes, there's actually a tiny electronic chip inside your U.S. passport. It stores information used to verify that the passport is authentic.
 Once your identity is verified and the setup is approved, your Digital ID appears in Apple Wallet.
 You can also present your Digital ID using a compatible Apple Watch.
 How to set up a digital ID on Android 
 Android users have a similar feature called ID Pass in Google Wallet.
 To create one:
 Open Google Wallet.
 Tap Add to Wallet.
 Select ID, then ID Pass.
 Scan your U.S. passport's photo page.
 Use your phone to read the passport's embedded chip.
 Complete the required facial verification.
 Once verification is complete, your ID Pass is available in Google Wallet.
 Neither option requires your state to participate in a digital driver's license program. Eligible travelers across the United States can create a passport-based digital ID.
 How does it work at airport security? 
 At a participating TSA checkpoint, you can hold your iPhone or Android phone near the identity reader, much like using your phone to pay at a grocery store.
 Your phone will prompt you to authenticate and approve sharing the requested identification information.
 You don't have to hand your phone to a TSA officer.
 The technology is designed to make identity verification more convenient while giving travelers control over the information they share.
 But there's a catch.
 I tested digital ID at three airports. Here's what happened. 
 Earlier this year, I tested digital identification at three different airports, and the experiences couldn't have been more different.
 At the first airport, it worked beautifully. I presented my phone, completed the verification, and was on my way.
 At the second airport, the process was painfully slow. It would have been much faster to simply hand over my driver's license.
 At the third airport, it didn't work at all.
 That's something travelers need to understand before relying on this technology during the busy Thanksgiving travel season.
 Even at airports equipped to accept digital identification, the process may not always work as expected.
 What if you don't have a REAL ID driver's license? 
 If you never got around to upgrading your driver's license to a REAL ID, a passport-based digital ID offers another option at participating TSA checkpoints for domestic travel.
 However, the TSA recommends carrying an acceptable physical form of identification, even if you plan to use a digital ID.
 A valid U.S. passport is an acceptable alternative to a REAL ID driver's license.
 And remember, a digital ID stored on your phone cannot replace your physical passport for international travel.
 Should you set it up before Thanksgiving? 
 Absolutely, especially if you already have a valid U.S. passport and a compatible smartphone.
 Setting up a digital ID takes only a few minutes for many travelers, although verification may take longer. It's one less thing you may have to pull out of your wallet when going through security.
 But based on my experience, I wouldn't rely on it as my only identification.
 The bottom line: Apple's Digital ID and Google's ID Pass are convenient when they work. Just make sure you have your physical driver's license or passport with you in case they don't.
 And if you're flying for Thanksgiving, that's one less surprise you'll want at the airport.
